### <span id="SECTION00532400000000000000">Saving a Result file</span>

<span id="936"> </span>

<span id="944"> </span><span id="resultPopup"> </span><img src="img106.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Figure:** Result File Popup\

A result file contains the activations of all output units. These activations are obtained by performing one pass of forward propagation. After pressing the <img src="img107.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> button a popup window lets the user select which patterns are to be tested and which patterns are to be saved in addition to the test output. Picture [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node38.html#resultPopup) shows that popup window. Since the result file has no meaning for the loaded network a load operation is not useful and therefore not supported.

\

### <span id="SECTION00532500000000000000">Defining the Log File</span>

<span id="951"> </span>

Messages that document the simulation run can be stored in the **log file**. The protocol contains file operations, definitions of values set by clicking the <img src="img108.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> button in the info panel, as well as a teaching protocol (cycles, parameters, errors). In addition, the user can output data about the network to the log file with the help of the info panel. If no log file is loaded, output takes place only on ` stdout`. If no file name is specified when clicking <img src="img109.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />, a possibly open log file is closed and further output is restricted to ` stdout`.

\

## <span id="SECTION00533000000000000000">Control Panel</span>

<span id="958"> </span> <span id="959"> </span> <span id="remPanel"> </span>

With this window the simulator is operated. Figure [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node40.html#ControlPanel) shows this window. Table [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node40.html#TabControlPanelItem) lists all the input options with types and value ranges. The meaning of the 5 learning parameters depends upon the learning function selected with the menu ` select learning function` invoked by the button <img src="img110.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> of the control panel.

<span id="972"> </span><span id="ControlPanel"> </span><img src="img111.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Figure:** Control Panel\

<span id="991"> </span><span id="TabControlPanelItem"> </span><img src="img112.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Table:** Input fields of the control panel\

There are the following text fields, buttons and menu buttons:

1.  ` STEPS`: This text field specifies the number of update steps of the network. With ` Topological_Order` selected as update mode (chosen with the menu ` select update function` from the button ` OPTIONS` in the control panel) one step is sufficient to propagate information from input to output. With other update modes or with recursive networks, several steps might be needed.

2.  <img src="img113.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: After clicking this button, the simulator kernel executes the number of steps specified in the text field ` STEPS`. If ` STEPS` is zero, the units are only redrawn. The update mode selected with the button <img src="img114.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> is used (see chapter [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node14.html#Modes)). The first update step in the mode ` topological` takes longer than the following, because the net is sorted topologically first. Then all units are redrawn.

3.  ` COUNT`: The text field next to the ` STEP` button displays the steps, executed so far.

4.  <img src="img115.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Initializes the network with values according to the function and parameters given in the last line of the panel.

5.  <img src="img116.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: The counter is reset and the units are assigned their initial activation.

6.  <img src="img117.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: <span id="1010"> </span> <span id="1011"> </span> By pressing the error button in the control panel, SNNS will print out several statistics. The formulas were contributed by Warren Sarle from the SAS institute. Note that these criteria are for *linear* models; they can sometimes be applied directly to nonlinear models if the sample size is large. A recommended reference for linear model selection criteria is \[[JGHL80](node389.html#Jud80)\].

    Notation:\

    <img src="img118.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

    **Criteria for adequacy of the estimated model in the sample**\
    Pearson's <img src="img119.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />, the proportion of variance, is explained or accounted by the model:\
    <img src="img120.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> **Criteria for adequacy of the true model in the population**\
    The mean square error \[[JGHL80](node389.html#Jud80)\] is defined as: <img src="img121.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />, the root mean square error as: <img src="img122.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />.

    The <img src="img123.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />, the <img src="img124.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> \[[JGHL80](node389.html#Jud80)\] adjusted for degrees of freedom, is defined as:\
    <img src="img125.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> **Criteria for adequacy of the estimated model in the population**\
    Anemiya's prediction criterion \[[JGHL80](node389.html#Jud80)\] is similar to the <img src="img126.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />:\
    <img src="img127.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />The estimated mean square error of prediction (<img src="img128.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />) assuming that the values of the regressors are fixed and that the model is correct is:\
    <img src="img129.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> The conservative mean square error in prediction \[[Weh94](node389.html#Weh94)\] is:\
    <img src="img130.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> The generalized cross validation (**GCV**) is given by Wahba \[[GHW79](node389.html#Gol79)\] as:\
    <img src="img131.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />The estimated mean square error of prediction assuming that both independent and dependent variables are multivariate normal is defined as:\
    <img src="img132.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />Shibata's criterion <img src="img133.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> can be found in \[[Shi68](node389.html#Shi81)\].

    Finally, there is Akaikes information criterion \[[JGHL80](node389.html#Jud80)\]:\
    <img src="img134.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />\
    and the Schwarz's Bayesian criterion \[[JGHL80](node389.html#Jud80)\]:\
    <img src="img135.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />.Obviously, most of these selection criteria do only make sense, if **n\>\>p**.

7.  <img src="img136.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Information about the net is written to the text window.

8.  ` CYCLES`: This text field specifies the number of learning cycles. It is mainly used in conjunction with the next two buttons. A cycle (also called an epoch sometimes) is a unit of training where all patterns of a pattern file are presented to the network once.

9.  <img src="img137.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: The net is trained with a single pattern for the number of training cycles defined in the field ` CYCLES`. The text window reports the error of the network every ` CYCLES`<img src="img138.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> cycles, i.e. independent of the number of training cycles only 10 numbers are generated. (This prevents flooding the user with network performance data and slowing down the training by file I/O).

    <span id="1076"> </span> The error reported in the text window is the sum of the quadratic differences between the teaching input and the real output over all output units. The average error per output unit is given behind ` ave`.

10. <img src="img139.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: The net is trained with all patterns for the number of training cycles specified in the field ` CYCLES`. This is the usual way to train networks from the graphical user interface. Note, that if cycles has a value of, say, 100, the button ` ALL` causes SNNS to train all patterns once (one cycle = one epoch) and repeat this 100 times (NOT training each pattern 100 times in a row and then applying the next pattern).

    The error reported in the text window is the sum of the quadratic difference between the teaching input and the real output over all output units summed over the number of patterns presented. The average error per output unit is given behind ` ave`.

11. <img src="img140.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Stops the teaching cycle. After completion of the current step or teaching cycle, the simulation is halted immediately.

12. <img src="img141.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: With this button, the user can test the behavior of the net with all patterns loaded. The activation values of input and output units are copied into the net. (For output units see also button <img src="img142.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />). Then the number of update steps specified in ` STEPS` are executed.

13. <img src="img143.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: It is important for optimal learning that the various patterns are presented in different order in the different cycles. A random sequence of patterns is created automatically, if ` SHUFFLE` is switched on.

14. <img src="img144.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Offers the following menu: <span id="1089"> </span>

    <img src="img145.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

    If ` jog weights` is selected, a popup window appears to specify the value range (` low limit .. high limit`) of the random noise to be added to all links in the network.

15. <img src="img146.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: With this button, the user specifies the changes to the activation values of the output units when a pattern is applied with <img src="img147.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />. The following table gives the three possible alternatives:

    <img src="img148.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

    The label of this button always displays the item selected from the menu.

16. ` PATTERN`: This text field displays the current pattern number.

17. <img src="img149.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: The pattern whose number is displayed in the text field ` PATTERN` is deleted from the pattern file.

18. <img src="img150.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: The pattern whose number is displayed in the text field ` PATTERN` is modified in place.

    The current activation of the input units and the current output values of output units of the network loaded make up the input and output pattern. These values might have been set with the network editor and the Info panel before.

19. <img src="img151.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: A new pattern is defined that is added behind existing patterns. Input and output values are defined as above. This button is disabled whenever the current pattern set has variable dimensions.

20. <img src="img152.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: The simulator advances to the pattern whose number is displayed in the text field ` PATTERN`.

21. Arrow buttons xgui_figs/xgui_button_first.ps, xgui_figs/xgui_button_prev.ps, xgui_figs/xgui_button_next.ps, and xgui_figs/xgui_button_last.ps: With these buttons, the user can navigate through all patterns loaded, as well as jump directly to the first and last pattern. Unlike with the button <img src="img153.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> no update steps are performed here.

22. <img src="img154.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Opens the panel for sub-pattern handling. The button is inactive when the current pattern set has no variable dimensions. The sub-pattern panel is described in section [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node106.html#varPat).

23. <img src="img155.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Opens the menu of loaded pattern sets. The pattern set of the selected entry is removed from main memory. The corresponding pattern file remains untouched. When the current pattern set is deleted, the last in the list becomes current. When the last remaining pattern set is deleted, the current pattern set becomes undefined and the menu shows the entry ` No Files`.

24. <img src="img156.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Also opens the menu of loaded pattern sets. The pattern set of the selected entry becomes the current set. All training, testing, and propagation actions refer always to the current pattern set. The name of the corresponding pattern file is displayed next to the button in the *Current Pattern Set* field.

25. *Current Pattern Set*: This field displays the name of the pattern set currently used for training. When no current pattern set is defined the entry "` Training Pattern File ?`" is displayed.

26. ` VALID`: Gives the intervals in which the training process is to be interrupted by the computation of the error on the validation pattern set. A value of 0 inhibits validation. The validation error is printed on the shell window and plotted in the graph display.

27. <img src="img157.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Opens the menu of loaded pattern sets. The pattern set of the selected entry becomes the current validation set. The name of the corresponding pattern file is displayed next to the button in the *Validation Pattern Set* field.

28. *Validation Pattern Set*: This field displays the name of the pattern set currently used for validation. When no current pattern set is defined the entry "` Validation Pattern File ?`" is displayed.

29. ` LEARN`: Up to five fields to specify the parameters of the learning function. The number required and their resp. meaning depend upon the learning function used. Only as many widgets as parameters needed will be displayed, i.e. all widgets visible need to filled in. A description of the learning functions that are already built in into SNNS is given in section [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node52.html#LearningParameters).

30. <img src="img158.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: in the LEARN row invokes a menu to select a learning function (learning procedure). The following learning functions are currently implemented: <span id="1139"> </span> <span id="1140"> </span>

    <img src="img159.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

    <img src="img160.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

31. ` UPDATE`: Up to five fields to specify the parameters of the update function. The number required and their resp. meaning depend upon the update function used. Only as many widgets as parameters needed will be displayed, i.e. all widgets visible need to filled in.

32. <img src="img161.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: in the UPDATE row invokes a menu to select an update function. A list of the update functions that are already built in into SNNS and their descriptions is given in section [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node53.html#UpdateFuncs).

33. ` INIT`: Five fields to specify the parameters of the init function. The number required and their resp. meaning depend upon the init function used. Only as many widgets as parameters needed will be displayed, i.e. all widgets visible need to filled in.

34. <img src="img162.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: in the INIT row invokes a menu to select an initialization function. See section [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node78.html#InitFuncs) for a list of the init functions available as well as their description.

## <span id="SECTION00534000000000000000">Info Panel</span>

<span id="UnitInfoPanel"> </span> <span id="1192"> </span> <span id="1193"> </span>

<span id="1201"> </span><span id="FigUnitInfoPanel"> </span><img src="img163.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Figure:** Info panel\

<span id="1205"> </span> <span id="1206"> </span> The info panel displays all data of two units and the link between them. The unit at the beginning of the link is called ` SOURCE`, the other ` TARGET`. One may run sequentially through all connections or sites of the ` TARGET` unit with the arrow buttons and look at the corresponding source units and vice versa.

This panel is also very important for editing, since some operations refer to the displayed ` TARGET` unit or (` SOURCE`<img src="img164.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />` TARGET`) link. A default unit can also be created here, whose values (activation, bias, IO-type, subnet number, layer numbers, activation function, and output function) are copied into all selected units of the net.

The source unit of a link can also be specified in a 2D display by pressing the middle mouse button, the target unit by releasing it. To select a link between two units the user presses the middle mouse button on the source unit in a 2D display, moves the mouse to the target unit while holding down the mouse button and releases it at the target unit. Now the selected units and their link are displayed in the info panel. If no link exists between two units selected in a 2D display, the ` TARGET` is displayed with its first link, thereby changing ` SOURCE`.

In table [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node41.html#InfoItems) the various fields are listed. The fields in the second line of the SOURCE or TARGET unit display the name of the activation function, name of the output function, name of the f-type (if available). The fields in the line ` LINK` have the following meaning: weight, site value, site function, name of the site. Most often only a link weight is available. In this case no information about sites is displayed.

<span id="1243"> </span><span id="InfoItems"> </span><img src="img165.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Table:** Table of the unit, link and site fields in the Info panel\

Unit number, unit subnet number, site value, and site function cannot be modified. To change attributes of type text, the cursor has to be exactly in the corresponding field.

There are the following buttons for the units (from left to right):

1.  Arrow button xgui_figs/xgui_button_first.ps: The button below TARGET selects the first target unit (of the given source unit); the button below SOURCE selects the first source unit (of the given target unit);

2.  Arrow button xgui_figs/xgui_button_next.ps: The button below TARGET selects the next target unit (of the given source unit); the button below SOURCE selects the next source unit (of the given target unit);

3.  <img src="img166.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Unit is frozen, if this button is inverted. Changes become active only after <img src="img167.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> is clicked.

4.  <img src="img168.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: The default unit is assigned the displayed values of ` TARGET` and ` SOURCE` (only activation, bias, IO-type, subnet number, layer numbers, activation function and output function).

5.  <img src="img169.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Calls the following menu:

    <img src="img170.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

6.  <img src="img171.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Only after clicking this button the attributes of the corresponding unit are set to the specified value. The unit is also redrawn. Therefore the values can be changed without immediate effect on the unit.

There exist the following buttons for links (from left to right):

1.  xgui_figs/xgui_button_first.ps: Select first link of the ` TARGET` unit.

2.  xgui_figs/xgui_button_next.ps: Select next link of the ` TARGET` unit.

3.  <img src="img172.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Calls the following menu:

    <img src="img173.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

4.  <img src="img174.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Only after clicking this button the link weight is set.

### <span id="SECTION00534100000000000000">Unit Function Displays</span>

<span id="1295"> </span> <span id="1296"> </span>

The characteristic functions of the units can be displayed in a graphic representation. For this purpose separate displays have been created, that can be called by selecting the options ` display activation function` or ` display output function` in the menu under the ` options` button of the target and source unit in the info panel.

<span id="2241"> </span><img src="img175.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Figure:** <span id="act_func2"> </span> The logistic activation function in a unit function display\

Figure [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node42.html#act_func2) shows an example of an activation function. The window header states whether it is an activation or an output function, as well as whether it is the current function of the source or target unit.

The size of the window is as flexible as the picture range of the displayed function. The picture range can be changed by using the dialog widgets at the top of the function displays. The size of the window may be changed by using the standard mechanisms of your window manager.

If a new activation or output function has been defined for the unit, the display window changes automatically to reflect the new situation. Thereby it is easy to get a quick overview of the available functions by opening the function displays and then clicking through the list of available functions (This list can be obtained by selecting ` select activation function` or ` select output function` in the unit menu).

\

## <span id="SECTION00535000000000000000">2D Displays</span>

<span id="GraphicWindows"> </span> <span id="1315"> </span> <span id="1316"> </span>

<span id="1317"> </span> A 2D display or simply display is always part of the user interface. It serves to display the network topology, the units' activations and the weights of the links. Each unit is located on a grid position, which simplifies the positioning of the units. The distance between two grid points (` grid width`) can be changed from the default 37 pixels to other values in the setup panel.

The current position, i.e. the grid position of the mouse, is also numerically displayed at the bottom of the manager panel. The x-axis is the horizontal line and valid coordinates lie in the range **-32736** ... **+32735** (short integer).

The current version displays units as boxes, where the size of the box is proportional to the value of the displayed attribute. Possible attributes are activation, initial activation, bias, and output. A black box represents a positive value, an empty box a negative value. The size of the unit varies between 16x16 and 0 pixels according to the value of **scaleFactor**. The parameter *scaleFactor* has a default value of <img src="img176.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />, but may be set to values between <img src="img177.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> and <img src="img178.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> in the setup panel. Each unit can be displayed with two of several attributes. One above the unit and one below the unit. The attributes to be displayed can be selected in the setup panel.

Links are shown as solid lines, with optional numerical display of the weight in the center of the line and/or arrow head pointing to the target unit. These features are optional, because they heavily affect the drawing speed of the display window.

A display can also be frozen with the button <img src="img179.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> (button gets inverted). It is afterwards neither updated anymore<a href="footnode.html#1321" id="tex2html127"><img src="icons/foot_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" /></a>, nor does it accept further editor commands.

An iconified display is not updated and therefore consumes (almost) no CPU time. If a window is closed, its dimensions and setup parameters are saved in a stack (LIFO). This means that a newly requested display gets the values of the window assigned that was last closed. For better orientation, the window title contains the subnet number which was specified for this display in the setup panel.

\

### <span id="SECTION00535100000000000000">Setup Panel of a 2D Display</span>

<span id="SetupPanel"> </span> <span id="1324"> </span> <span id="1325"> </span>

Changes to the kind of display of the network can be performed in the **Setup panel**. All settings become valid only after the button <img src="img180.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> is clicked. The whole display window is then redrawn.

<span id="1335"> </span><span id="FigSetupPanel"> </span><img src="img181.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Figure:** Setup Panel of a 2D-display.\

1.  <span id="1340"> </span>

2.  Buttons to control the display of unit information: The first two lines of the Setup panel (` units top` and ` units bottom`) contain two buttons each to set the unit parameter that can be displayed at the top resp. the bottom of the unit.

    The button <img src="img182.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> toggles the display of information which can be selected with the button <img src="img183.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />. The unit name, unit number, or the z-value (3D coordinate) can be displayed above the unit, the activation, initial activation, bias, or output of the unit below the unit. The numerical attribute selected with the button <img src="img184.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> at the bottom of the unit (activation, initial activation, output, or bias) also determines the size of the unit in the graphical representation.

    It is usually not advisable to switch off ` top` (number or name), because this information is needed for reference to the info panel. An unnamed unit is always displayed with its number.

    <span id="1347"> </span>

3.  Buttons to control the display of link information: The third line consists of three buttons to select the display of link data, <img src="img185.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />, <img src="img186.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />, <img src="img187.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.
    - <img src="img188.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> determines whether to draw links at all (then <img src="img189.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> is inverted),
    - <img src="img190.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> displays link weights at the center of the line representing the link,
    - <img src="img191.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> displays arrow heads of the links pointing from source to target unit.

    <span id="1357"> </span>

4.  <img src="img192.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> invokes another popup window to select the display of up to eight different layers in the display window. Layers are being stacked like transparent sheets of paper and allow for a selective display of units and links. These layers need NOT correspond with layers of units of the network topology (as in multilayer feed-forward networks), but they may do so. Layers are very useful to display only a selected subset of the network. The display of each layer can be switched on or off independently. A unit may belong to several layers at the same time. The assignment of units to layers can be done with the menu ` assign layers` invoked with the button ` OPTIONS` in the main Info panel.
    <span id="1361"> </span>

5.  <img src="img193.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> sets the 2D--display colors. On monochrome terminals, black on white or white on black representation of the network can be selected from a popup menu. On color displays, a color editing window is opened. This window consists of three parts: The palette of available colors at the top, the buttons to select the item to be colored in the lower left region, and the color preview window in the lower right region.

    <span id="1370"> </span><img src="img194.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
    **Figure:** Color Setup Panel.\

    A color is set by clicking first at the appropriate button (<img src="img195.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />, <img src="img196.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />, or <img src="img197.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />) and then at the desired color in the color palette. The selected setting is immediately displayed in the color preview window. All colors may be set in any order and any number of times. The changes become effective in the corresponding 2D--display only after both the setup panel and the color edit panel have been dismissed with the <img src="img198.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> button.

    <span id="1377"> </span>

6.  Sliders for the selection of link display parameters, ` links positive` and ` links negative`:

    There are two slidebars to set thresholds for the display of links. When the bubble is moved, the current threshold is displayed in absolute and relative value at the bottom of the setup panel. Only those links with an absolute value above the threshold are displayed. The range of the absolute values is <img src="img199.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> (see also paragraph [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node43.html#GraphicWindows)). The trigger values can be set independently for positive and negative weights. With these link thresholds the user can concentrate on the strong connections. Reducing the number of links drawn is an effective means to speed up the drawing of the displays, since line drawing takes most of the time to display a network.

    Note: The links that are not drawn are only invisible. They still remain accessible, i.e. they are affected by editor operations.

    <span id="1381"> </span>

7.  ` units scale`: This slidebar sets the parameter *scaleFactor* for the size of the growing boxes of the units. Its range is <img src="img200.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />. A scale factor of <img src="img201.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> draws the unit with activation <img src="img202.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> with full size. A scale factor of <img src="img203.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> draws a unit with activation <img src="img204.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> only with half size.
    <span id="1384"> </span>

8.  ` grid width`: This value sets the width of the grid on which the units are placed. For some nets, changing the default of 37 pixels may be useful, e.g. to be able to better position the units in a geometrical pattern. Overlapping tops and bottoms occur if a grid size of less than 35 pixels is selected (26 pixels if units are displayed without numerical values). This overlap, however, does not affect computation in any way.
    <span id="1386"> </span>

9.  ` origin (grid)`: These two fields determine the origin of the window, i.e. the grid position of the top left corner. There, the left field represents the x coordinate, the right is the y coordinate. The origin is usually (0, 0). Setting it to (20, 0) moves the display 20 units to the right and 10 units down in the grid.
    <span id="1388"> </span>

10. ` subnet number`: This field adjusts the subnet number to be displayed in this window. Values between **-32736** and **+32735** are possible here.

## <span id="SECTION00536000000000000000">Graph Window</span>

<span id="1392"> </span> <span id="1393"> </span> <span id="1394"> </span> Graph is a tool to visualize the error development of a net. The program is started by clicking the <img src="img205.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> button in the manager panel or by typing Alt-g in any SNNS window. Figure [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node45.html#errorGraph1) shows the window of the graph tool.

<span id="1404"> </span><span id="errorGraph1"> </span><img src="img206.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Figure:** Graph window\

Graph is only active after calling it. This means, the development of the error is only drawn as long as the window is not closed. The advantage of this implementation is, that the simulator is not slowed down as long as graph is closed<a href="footnode.html#1408" id="tex2html145"><img src="icons/foot_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" /></a>. If the window is iconified, graph remains active.

The error curve of the net is plotted until the net is initialized or a new net is loaded, in which case the cycle counter is reset to zero. The window, however, is not cleared until the clear button is pressed. This opens the possibility to compare several error curves in a single display (see also figure [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node45.html#errorGraph1)). The maximum number of curves, which can be displayed simultaneously is 25. If a <img src="img207.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> curve is tried to be drawn, the confirmer appears with an error message.

When the curve reaches the right end of the window, an automatic rescale of the x-axis is performed. This way, the whole curve always remains visible.

In the top region of the graph window, seven buttons for handling the display are located:

<img src="img208.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Clears the screen of the graph window and sets the cycle counter to zero.

<img src="img209.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Closes the graph window and resets the cycle counter.

For both the x-- and y--axis the following two buttons are available:

xgui_figs/xgui_button_prev.ps: Reduce scale in one direction.

xgui_figs/xgui_button_next.ps: Enlarge scale in one direction.

<img src="img210.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Opens a popup menu to select the value to be plotted. Choices are <img src="img211.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />, <img src="img212.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />, and <img src="img213.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />, the SSE divided by the number of output units.

While the simulator is working all buttons are blocked.

The graph window can be resized by the mouse like every X-window. Changing the size of the window does not change the size of the scale.

When validation is turned on in the control panel two curves will be drawn simultaneously in the graph window, one for the training set and one for the validation set. On color terminals the validation error will be plotted as solid red line, on B/W terminals as dashed black line.

## <span id="SECTION00537000000000000000">Weight Display</span>

<span id="1422"> </span> <span id="1423"> </span>

<span id="2242"> </span><img src="img214.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Figure:** <span id="Hinton"> </span> A typical Hinton diagram\

The weight display window is a separate window specialized for displaying the weights of a network. It is called from the manager panel with the <img src="img215.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> button, or by typing Alt-w in any snns window. On black-and-white screens the weights are represented as squares with changing size in a Hinton diagram, while on color screens, fixed size squares with changing colors (WV-diagrams) are used. It can be used to analyze the weight distribution, or to observe the weight development during learning.

Initially the window has a size of 400x400 pixel.The weights are represented by <img src="img216.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> pixels on B/W and <img src="img217.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> pixels on color terminals. If the net is small, the square sizes are automatically enlarged to fill up the window. If the weights do not fit into the window, the scrollbars attached to the window allow scrolling over the display.

These settings may be changed by the user by pressing the <img src="img218.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> and <img src="img219.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> buttons in the upper part of the window. <img src="img220.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> enlarges the weight square by one pixel on each side, while <img src="img221.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> shrinks it.

The setup panel lets the user change the look of the display further. Here the width of the underlying grid can be changed. If the grid size is bigger than the number of connections in the network, no grid will be displayed. Also the color scale (resp. size scale for B/W) can be changed here. The initial settings correspond to the SNNS variables ` max_weight` and ` min_weight`.

<span id="1441"> </span> In a Hinton diagram, the size of a square corresponds to the absolute size of the correlated link. A filled square represents positive, an square frame negative links. The maximum size of the squares is computed automatically, to allow an optimal use of the display. <span id="1442"> </span> In a WV diagram color is used to code the value of a link. Here, a bright red is used for large negative values and a bright green is used for positive values. Intermediate numbers have a lighter color and the value zero is represented by white. A reference color scale is displayed in the top part of the window. The user also has the possibility to display the numerical value of the link by clicking any mouse button while the mouse pointer is on the square. A popup window then gives source and target unit of the current link as well as its weight.

For a better overall orientation the numbers of the units are printed all around the display and a grid with user definable size is used. In this numbering the units on top of the screen represent source units, while numbers to the left and right represent target units.

## <span id="SECTION00538000000000000000">Projection Panel</span>

<span id="1444"> </span> <span id="1445"> </span>

<span id="2243"> </span><img src="img222.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Figure:** PROJECTION panel for the 2-spirals problem. Note that the input range of the X and Y units must be specified, not the output range. In contrast, the output range of the third unit specified determines the color. Here the following values have been used: X-axis: unit 1 value range -6.5 to 6.5; Y-axis: unit 2 value range -6.5 to 6.5; activation pattern: unit 38 (the only output unit of the network) value range 0 to 1 <span id="ProjectionPanel"> </span>\

The projection analysis tool allows to display how the output of one unit (e.g. a hidden or an output unit) depends on two input units. It thus realizes a projection to two input vector axes.

It can be called by clicking the <img src="img223.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> button in the manager panel or by typing Alt-p in any SNNS window. The display of the projection panel is similar to the weights display, from which it is derived.

in the setup panel, two units must be specified, whose inputs are varied over the given input value range to give the X resp. Y coordinate of the projection display. The third unit to be specified is the one whose output value determines the color of the points with the given X and Y coordinate values. The range for the color coding can be specified as output range. For the most common logistic activation function this range is <img src="img224.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />.

The use of the other buttons, <img src="img225.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />, <img src="img226.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> and <img src="img227.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> are analogous to the weight display and should be obvious.

The projection tool is very instructive with the 2-spirals problem, the XOR problem or similar problems with two-dimensional input. Each hidden unit or output unit can be inspected and it can be determined, to which part of the input space the neuron is sensitive. Comparing different networks trained for such a problem by visualizing to which part of the input space they are sensitive gives insights about the internal representation of the networks and sometimes also about characteristics of the training algorithms used for training. A display of the projection panel is given in figure [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node47.html#ProjectionPanel).

## <span id="SECTION00539000000000000000">Print Panel</span>

<span id="PrintPanel"> </span> <span id="1464"> </span> <span id="1465"> </span>

The print panel handles the Postscript output. A 2D-display can be associated with the printer. All setup options and values of this display will be printed. Color and encapsulated Postscript are also supported. The output device is either a printer or a file. If the output device is a printer, a '.ps'-file is generated and spooled in the /tmp directory. It has a unique name starting with the prefix \`snns'. The directory must be writable. When xgui terminates normally, all SNNS spool files are deleted.

<span id="1473"> </span><span id="FigPrintPanel"> </span><img src="img228.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Figure:** Printer panel\

The following fields can be set in the Printer Panel, which is shown in figure [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node48.html#FigPrintPanel).

1.  **File Name** resp. **Command Line**:\
    If the output device is a file: the filename.\
    If the output device is a printer: the command line to start the printer.\
    The filename in the command line has to be '\$1'.
2.  **Destination**: Selects the output device. Toggles the above input line between File Name and Command Line.
3.  **Paper**: Selects the paper format.
4.  **Orientation**: Sets the orientation of the display on the paper. Can be 'portrait' or 'landscape'.
5.  **Border (mm)**: Sets the size of the horizontal and vertical borders on the sheet in millimeters.
6.  **AutoScale**: Scales the network to the largest size possible on the paper.
7.  **Aspect**: If on, scaling in X and Y direction is done uniformly.
8.  **X-Scale**: Scale factor in X direction. Valid only if AutoScale is 'OFF'.
9.  **Y-Scale**: Scale factor in Y direction. Valid only if AutoScale is 'OFF'.

<img src="img229.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Cancels the printing and closes the panel.

<img src="img230.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Starts printing.

<img src="img231.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Opens the network setup panel. This panel allows the specification of several options to control the way the network is printed. <span id="1493"> </span> <span id="1494"> </span>

The variables that can be set here include:

1.  **x-min**, **y-min**, **x-max** and **y-max** describe the section to be printed.

2.  ` `**`Unit size`**`:¯ `<img src="img232.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />`: All units have the same size. `

    <img src="img233.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: The size of a unit depends on its value.

3.  **Shape**: Sets the shape of the units.

4.  ` `**`Text`**`:¯ `<img src="img234.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />`: The box around text overwrites the background color and the links. `

    <img src="img235.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: No box around the text.

5.  **Border**: A border is drawn around the network, if set to 'ON'.

6.  **Color**: If set, the value is printed color coded.

7.  **Fill Intens**: The fill intensity for units on monochrome printers.

8.  **Display**: Selects the display to be printed.

## <span id="SECTION005310000000000000000">Help Windows</span>

<span id="HelpWindows"> </span> <span id="1518"> </span> <span id="1519"> </span>

An arbitrary number of help windows may be opened, each displaying a different part of the text. For a display of context sensitive help about the editor commands, the mouse must be in a display and the key <img src="img236.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> must be pressed. Then the last open help window appears with a short description.

<span id="1528"> </span><span id="FigHelpWindow"> </span><img src="img237.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Figure:** Help Window\

A special feature is the possibility of searching a given string in the help text. For this, the search string is selected in the text window (e.g. by a double click).

1.  <img src="img238.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: After clicking this button, SNNS looks for the first appearance of the marked string, starting at the beginning of the help document. If the string is found, the corresponding paragraph is displayed.
2.  <img src="img239.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: After clicking this button, SNNS looks for the first appearance of the marked string, starting at the position last visited by a call to the help function. If the text was scrolled afterwards, this position might not be on the display anymore.

<span id="1536"> </span> Note: All help calls look for the first appearance of a certain string. These strings start with the sequence ASTERISK-BLANK (`* `), to assure the discovery of the appropriate text position. With this knowledge it is easy to modify the file ` help.hdoc` to adapt it to special demands, like storing information about unit types or patterns. The best approach would be to list all relevant keywords at the end of the file under the headline \`\`` * TOPICS`'', so that the user can select this directory by a click to <img src="img240.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.

## <span id="SECTION005311000000000000000">Shell window</span>

The window of the shell from which SNNS is invoked is used for the output of protocol messages.

These protocols include:

- Messages about the success or failure of the loading or saving of a file.
- Information about the settings of SNNS when the <img src="img241.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> button in the control panel is pressed.
- Error messages of the pattern file parser when the pattern file does not correspond to the required grammar.
- Learning error values (see below)
- Validation set error values

When learning is started, the error of the output units is reported on this window after each epoch, i.e. after the presentation of all patterns.

To save the window from being flooded on longer training runs, the maximum number of reported errors is limited to 10. Therefore, when 20 learning cycles are specified, the error gets printed only after every other cycle. This error report has the following form:

Learning all patterns: epochs : 100 parameter: 0.80000 \#o-units : 26 \#patterns: 26 epoch: SSE MSE SSE/o-units Train 100: 57.78724 2.22259 2.22259 Train 90: 24.67467 0.94903 0.94903 Train 80: 23.73399 0.91285 0.91285 Train 70: 22.40005 0.86154 0.86154 Train 60: 20.42843 0.78571 0.78571 Train 50: 18.30172 0.70391 0.70391 Test 50: 25.34673 0.97487 0.97487 Train 40: 16.57888 0.63765 0.63765 Train 30: 14.84296 0.57088 0.57088 Train 20: 12.97301 0.49896 0.49896 Train 10: 11.22209 0.43162 0.43162 Train 1: 10.03500 0.38596 0.38596 Test 1: 11.13500 0.42696 0.42696

The first line reports whether all or only a single pattern is trained. The next lines give the number of specified cycles and the given learning parameters, followed by a brief setup description.

Then the 10-row-table of the learning progress is given. If validation is turned on this table is intermixed with the output of the validation. The first column specifies whether the displayed error is computed on the training or validation pattern set, \`\`Test'' is printed for the latter case. The second column gives the number of epochs still to be processed. The third column is the Sum Squared Error (SSE) of the learning function. It is computed with the following formula:

<img src="img242.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

where <img src="img243.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is the teaching output (desired output) of output neuron j on pattern p and <img src="img244.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is the actual output. The forth column is the Mean Squared Error (MSE), which is the SSE divided by the number of patterns. The fifth value finally gives the SSE divided by the number of output units.

The second and third values are equal if there are as many patterns as there are output units (e.g. the letters network), the first and third values are identical, if the network has only one output unit (e.g. the xor network).

If the training of the network is interrupted by pressing the <img src="img245.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> button in the control panel, the values for the last completed training cycle are reported.

## <span id="SECTION005312000000000000000">Confirmer</span>

<span id="Confirmer"> </span> <span id="1553"> </span>

<span id="1570"> </span><span id="FigConfirmer"> </span><img src="img246.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />\
**Figure:** A normal confirmer and a message confirmer.\

The confirmer is a window where the graphical user interface displays important information or requires the user to confirm destructive operations. The confirmer always appears in the middle of the screen and blocks XGUI until a button of the confirmer is clicked (see figure [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node51.html#FigConfirmer)).

# <span id="SECTION00540000000000000000">Parameters of the Learning Functions</span>

<span id="LearningParameters"> </span> <span id="1577"> </span>

The following learning parameters (from left to right) are used by the learning functions that are already built into SNNS:

- ` Std_Backpropagation` (''Vanilla\`\` Backpropagation),\
  ` BackpropBatch` and\
  ` TimeDelayBackprop` <span id="1582"> </span> <span id="1583"> </span> <span id="1584"> </span> <span id="1585"> </span> <span id="1586"> </span> <span id="1587"> </span>
  1.  <img src="img247.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning parameter, specifies the step width of the gradient descent.

      Typical values of <img src="img248.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> are <img src="img249.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />. Some small examples actually train even faster with values above 1, like 2.0.

  2.  <img src="img250.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: the maximum difference <img src="img251.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> between a teaching value <img src="img252.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> and an output <img src="img253.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> of an output unit which is tolerated, i.e. which is propagated back as <img src="img254.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />. If values above 0.9 should be regarded as 1 and values below 0.1 as 0, then <img src="img255.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> should be set to <img src="img256.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />. This prevents overtraining of the network.

      Typical values of <img src="img257.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> are 0, 0.1 or 0.2.

- ` BackpropMomentum` (Backpropagation with momentum term and flat spot elimination): <span id="1600"> </span> <span id="1601"> </span>

  1.  <img src="img258.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning parameter, specifies the step width of the gradient descent.

      Typical values of <img src="img259.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> are <img src="img260.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />. Some small examples actually train even faster with values above 1, like 2.0.

  2.  <img src="img261.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: momentum term, specifies the amount of the old weight change (relative to 1) which is added to the current change.

      Typical values of <img src="img262.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> are <img src="img263.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.

  3.  **c**: flat spot elimination value, a constant value which is added to the derivative of the activation function to enable the network to pass flat spots of the error surface.

      Typical values of **c** are <img src="img264.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />, most often 0.1 is used.

  4.  <img src="img265.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: the maximum difference <img src="img266.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> between a teaching value <img src="img267.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> and an output <img src="img268.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> of an output unit which is tolerated, i.e. which is propagated back as <img src="img269.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />. See above.

  <span id="1611"> </span> The general formula for Backpropagation used here is

  <img src="img270.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

- ` BackpropWeightDecay` (Backpropagation with Weight Decay) <span id="1634"> </span> <span id="1635"> </span>
  1.  <img src="img271.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning parameter, specifies the step width of the gradient descent.

      Typical values of <img src="img272.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> are <img src="img273.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />. Some small examples actually train even faster with values above 1, like 2.0.

  2.  **d**: weight decay term, specifies how much of the old weight value is subtracted after learning. Try values between 0.005 and 0.3.

  3.  <img src="img274.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: the minimum weight that is tolerated for a link. All links with a smaller weight will be pruned.

  4.  <img src="img275.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: the maximum difference <img src="img276.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> between a teaching value <img src="img277.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> and an output <img src="img278.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> of an output unit which is tolerated, i.e. which is propagated back as <img src="img279.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />. See above.

- ` BackpropThroughTime (BPTT)`,\
  ` BatchBackpropThroughTime (BBPTT)`: <span id="1648"> </span> <span id="1649"> </span> <span id="1650"> </span> <span id="1651"> </span>
  1.  <img src="img280.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning parameter, specifies the step width of the gradient descent.

      Typical values of <img src="img281.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> for BPTT and BBPTT are <img src="img282.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.

  2.  <img src="img283.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: momentum term, specifies the amount of the old weight change (relative to 1) which is added to the current change.

      Typical values of <img src="img284.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> are <img src="img285.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.

  3.  backstep: the number of backprop steps back in time. BPTT stores a sequence of all unit activations while input patterns are applied. The activations are stored in a first-in-first-out queue for each unit. The largest backstep value supported is 10.

- ` Quickprop`: <span id="1655"> </span> <span id="1656"> </span>
  1.  <img src="img286.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning parameter, specifies the step width of the gradient descent.

      Typical values of <img src="img287.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> for Quickprop are <img src="img288.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.

  2.  <img src="img289.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: maximum growth parameter, specifies the maximum amount of weight change (relative to 1) which is added to the current change

      Typical values of <img src="img290.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> are <img src="img291.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.

  3.  <img src="img292.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: weight decay term to shrink the weights.

      Typical values of <img src="img293.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> are <img src="img294.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />. Quickprop is rather sensitive to this parameter. It should not be set too large.

  4.  <img src="img295.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: the maximum difference <img src="img296.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> between a teaching value <img src="img297.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> and an output <img src="img298.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> of an output unit which is tolerated, i.e. which is propagated back as <img src="img299.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />. See above.

- ` QuickpropThroughTime (QPTT)`: <span id="1667"> </span> <span id="1668"> </span>
  1.  <img src="img300.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning parameter, specifies the step width of the gradient descent.

      Typical values of <img src="img301.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> for QPTT are <img src="img302.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.

  2.  <img src="img303.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: maximum growth parameter, specifies the maximum amount of weight change (relative to 1) which is added to the current change

      Typical values of <img src="img304.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> are <img src="img305.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.

  3.  <img src="img306.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: weight decay term to shrink the weights.

      Typical values of <img src="img307.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> are <img src="img308.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.

  4.  backstep: the number of quickprop steps back in time. QPTT stores a sequence of all unit activations while input patterns are applied. The activations are stored in a first-in-first-out queue for each unit.

      The largest backstep value supported is 10.

- ` Counterpropagation`: <span id="1672"> </span> <span id="1673"> </span>
  1.  <img src="img309.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: learning parameter of the Kohonen layer.

      Typical values of <img src="img310.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> for Counterpropagation are <img src="img311.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> .

  2.  <img src="img312.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning parameter of the Grossberg layer.

      Typical values of <img src="img313.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> are <img src="img314.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.

  3.  <img src="img315.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: threshold of a unit.

      We often use a value <img src="img316.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> of 0.

- ` Backpercolation 1`: <span id="1677"> </span> <span id="1678"> </span>
  1.  <img src="img317.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: global error magnification. This is the factor in the formula <img src="img318.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />, where <img src="img319.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> is the internal activation error of a unit, **t** is the teaching input and **o** the output of a unit.

      Typical values of <img src="img320.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> are 1. Bigger values (up to 10) may also be used here.

  2.  <img src="img321.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: If the error value <img src="img322.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> drops below this threshold value, the adaption according to the Backpercolation algorithm begins. <img src="img323.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is defined as:

      <img src="img324.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

  3.  <img src="img325.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: the maximum difference <img src="img326.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> between a teaching value <img src="img327.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> and an output <img src="img328.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> of an output unit which is tolerated, i.e. which is propagated back as <img src="img329.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />. See above.

- ` Dynamic Learning Vector Quantization (DLVQ)`: <span id="1691"> </span> <span id="1692"> </span>
  1.  <img src="img330.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning rate, specifies the step width of the mean vector <img src="img331.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />, which is nearest to a pattern <img src="img332.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />, towards this pattern. Remember that <img src="img333.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is moved only, if <img src="img334.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is not assigned to the correct class <img src="img335.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />. A typical value is 0.03.
  2.  <img src="img336.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning rate, specifies the step width of a mean vector <img src="img337.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />, to which a pattern of class <img src="img338.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is falsely assigned to, away from this pattern. A typical value is 0.03. Best results can be achieved, if the condition <img src="img339.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is satisfied.
  3.  Number of cycles you want to train the net before additive mean vectors are calculated.

- ` RadialBasisLearning`: <span id="1707"> </span> <span id="1708"> </span>
  1.  *centers*: determines the learning rate <img src="img340.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> used for the modification of center vectors.
  2.  *bias (p)*: determines the learning rate <img src="img341.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />, used for the modification of the parameters **p** of the base function. **p** is stored as bias of the hidden units.
  3.  *weights*: influences the training of all link weights that are leading to the output layer as well as the training of the bias of all output neurons.
  4.  *delta max.*: If the actual error is smaller than the maximum allowed error ( *delta max.*) the corresponding weights are not changed.
  5.  *momentum*:influences the amount of the momentum--term during training.

- ` RadialBasisLearning with Dynamic Decay Adjustment`: <span id="1718"> </span> <span id="1719"> </span>
  1.  <img src="img342.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: positive threshold. To commit a new prototype, none of the existing RBFs of the correct class may have an activation above <img src="img343.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />
  2.  <img src="img344.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />:negative threshold. During shrinking no RBF unit of a conflicting class is allowed to have an activation above <img src="img345.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.
  3.  n: the maximum number of RBF units to be diplayed in one row. This item allows the user to control the appearance of the network on the screen and has no influence on the performance.

- ` ART1` <span id="1727"> </span> <span id="1728"> </span>
  1.  <img src="img346.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: vigilance parameter. If the quotient of active F<img src="img347.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> units divided by the number of active F<img src="img348.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> units is below <img src="img349.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />, an ART reset is performed.

- ` ART2` <span id="1732"> </span> <span id="1733"> </span>
  1.  <img src="img350.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: vigilance parameter. Specifies the minimal length of the error vector **r** (units <img src="img351.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />).
  2.  **a**: Strength of the influence of the lower level in F<img src="img352.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> by the middle level.
  3.  **b**: Strength of the influence of the middle level in F<img src="img353.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> by the upper level.
  4.  **c**: Part of the length of vector **p** (units <img src="img354.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />) used to compute the error.
  5.  <img src="img355.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: Threshold for output function **f** of units <img src="img356.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> and <img src="img357.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />.

- ` ARTMAP` <span id="1739"> </span> <span id="1740"> </span>
  1.  <img src="img358.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: vigilance parameter for <img src="img359.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> subnet. (quotient <img src="img360.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />)
  2.  <img src="img361.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: vigilance parameter for <img src="img362.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> subnet. (quotient <img src="img363.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />)
  3.  <img src="img364.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: vigilance parameter for inter ART reset control. (quotient <img src="img365.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />)

- ` RPROP (resilient propagation)` <span id="1752"> </span> <span id="1753"> </span>
  1.  *delta<img src="img366.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />*: starting values for all <img src="img367.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />. Default value is 0.1.
  2.  *<img src="img368.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />*: the upper limit for the update values <img src="img369.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />.The default value of <img src="img370.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is <img src="img371.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.
  3.  *<img src="img372.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />*: the weight-decay determines the relationship between the output error and to reduction in the size of the weights. *Important:* Please note that the weight decay parameter <img src="img373.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> denotes the exponent, to allow comfortable input of very small weight-decay. A choice of the third learning parameter <img src="img374.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> corresponds to a ratio of weight decay term to output error of <img src="img375.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />.

- ` Cascade Correlation (CC)` and\
  ` Recurrent Cascade Correlation (RCC)` <span id="1765"> </span> <span id="1766"> </span>

  CC and RCC are not learning functions themselves. They are meta algorithms to build and train optimal networks. However, they have a set of standard learning functions embedded. Here these functions require modified parameters. The embedded learning functions are:

  - 

  - Backpropagation (in CC or RCC):

    1.  <img src="img376.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning parameter, specifies the step width of gradient decent minimizing the net error.
    2.  <img src="img377.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: momentum term, specifies the amount of the old weight change, which is added to the current change.
    3.  **c**: flat spot elimination value, a constant value which is added to the derivative of the activation function to enable the network to pass flat spots on the error surface.
    4.  <img src="img378.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning parameter, specifies the step width of gradient ascent maximizing the covariance.
    5.  <img src="img379.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: momentum term specifies the amount of the old weight change, which is added to the current change.

    The general formula for this learning function is:

    <img src="img380.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

    The slopes <img src="img381.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> and <img src="img382.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> are abbreviated by **S**. This abbreviation is valid for all embedded functions. By changing the sign of the gradient value <img src="img383.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />, the same learning function can be used to maximize the covariance and to minimize the error.

  - Rprop (in CC or RCC):

    1.  <img src="img384.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: decreasing factor, specifies the factor by which the update-value <img src="img385.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is to be decreased when minimizing the net error. A typical value is <img src="img386.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.
    2.  <img src="img387.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: increasing factor, specifies the factor by which the update-value <img src="img388.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is to be increased when minimizing the net error. A typical value is <img src="img389.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />
    3.  not used.
    4.  <img src="img390.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: decreasing factor, specifies the factor by which the update-value <img src="img391.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is to be decreased when maximizing the covariance. A typical value is <img src="img392.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.
    5.  <img src="img393.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: increasing factor, specifies the factor by which the update-value <img src="img394.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is to be increased when maximizing the covariance. A typical value is <img src="img395.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

    The weight change is computed by:

    <img src="img396.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

    where <img src="img397.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is defined as follows: <img src="img398.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />. Furthermore, the condition <img src="img399.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> should not be violated.

  - Quickprop (in CC or RCC):

    1.  <img src="img400.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning parameter, specifies the step width of the gradient descent when minimizing the net error. A typical value is <img src="img401.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />
    2.  <img src="img402.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: maximum growth parameter, realizes a kind of dynamic momentum term. A typical value is 2.0.
    3.  <img src="img403.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />: weight decay term to shrink the weights. A typical value is <img src="img404.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />.
    4.  <img src="img405.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning parameter, specifies the step width of the gradient ascent when maximizing the covariance. A typical value is <img src="img406.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />
    5.  <img src="img407.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: maximum growth parameter, realizes a kind of dynamic momentum term. A typical value is 2.0.

    The formula used is:

    <img src="img408.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

- ` Kohonen` <span id="1849"> </span> <span id="1850"> </span> <span id="1851"> </span>
  1.  *h(0):* Adaptation height. The initial adaptation height can vary between 0 and 1. It determines the overall adaptation strength.
  2.  *r(0):* Adaptation radius. The initial adaptation radius <img src="img409.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> is the radius of the neighborhood of the winning unit. All units within this radius are adapted. Values should range between 1 and the size of the map.
  3.  *mult_H:* Decrease factor. The adaptation height decreases monotonically after the presentation of every learning pattern. This decrease is controlled by the decrease factor mult_H: <img src="img410.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />
  4.  *mult_R:* Decrease factor. The adaptation radius also decreases monotonically after the presentation of every learning pattern. This second decrease is controlled by the decrease factor mult_R: <img src="img411.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />
  5.  *h:* Horizontal size. Since the internal representation of a network doesn't allow to determine the 2-dimensional layout of the grid, the horizontal size in units must be provided for the learning function. It is the same value as used for the creation of the network.

- ` RM_delta (Rumelhart and McClelland's delta rule) ` <span id="1860"> </span>
  1.  *n:* learning parameter, specifies the step width of the gradient descent. In \[[RM86](node389.html#rum861)\] Rumelhart and McClelland use 0.01, although values less than 0.03 are generally acceptable.
  2.  *Ncycles:* number of update cycles, specifies how many times a pattern is propagated through the network before the learning rule is applied. This parameter must be large enough so that the network is relatively stable after the set number of propagations. A value of 50 is recommended as a baseline. Increasing the value of this parameter increases the accuracy of the network but at a cost of processing time. Larger networks will probably require a higher setting of Ncycles.

  **NOTE:** With this learning rule the update function ` RM_Synchronous` has to be used which needs as update parameter the number of iterations!

- ` Hebbian Learning` <span id="1869"> </span>

  1.  *n:* learning parameter, specifies the step width of the gradient descent. Values less than (1 / number of nodes) are recommended.
  2.  *Wmax:* maximum weight strength, specifies the maximum absolute value of weight allowed in the network. A value of 1.0 is recommended, although this should be lowered if the network experiences explosive growth in the weights and activations. Larger networks will require lower values of Wmax.
  3.  *count:* number of times the network is updated before calculating the error.

  **NOTE:** With this learning rule the update function ` RM_Synchronous` has to be used which needs as update parameter the number of iterations!

- ` Monte-Carlo:` <span id="1878"> </span> <span id="1879"> </span>
  1.  ***Min***: lower limit of weights and biases. Typical values are <img src="img412.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />.
  2.  ***Max***: upper limit of weights and biases. Typical values are <img src="img413.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.

- ` Simulated_Annealing_SS_error`,\
  ` Simulated_Annealing_WTA_error` and\
  ` Simulated_Annealing_WWTA_error:` <span id="1887"> </span> <span id="1888"> </span> <span id="1889"> </span> <span id="1890"> </span> <span id="1891"> </span> <span id="1892"> </span>
  1.  ***Min***: lower limit of weights and biases. Typical values are <img src="img414.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />.
  2.  ***Max***: upper limit of weights and biases. Typical values are <img src="img415.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.
  3.  <img src="img416.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />: learning parameter, specifies the Simulated Annealing start temperature . Typical values of <img src="img417.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> are <img src="img418.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.
  4.  **deg**: degradation term of the temperature: <img src="img419.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> Typical values of **deg** are <img src="img420.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />.

- ` Scaled Conjugate Gradient (SCG)` <span id="1900"> </span> <span id="1901"> </span>

  All of the following parameters are non-critical, i.e. they influence only the speed of convergence, not whether there will be success or not.

  1.  <img src="img421.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />. Should satisfy <img src="img422.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />. If 0, will be set to <img src="img423.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />;

# <span id="SECTION00550000000000000000">Update Functions</span>

<span id="UpdateFuncs"> </span> <span id="1915"> </span>

Why is an update mode important? It is necessary to visit the neurons of a net in a specific sequential order to perform operations on them. This order depends on the topology of the net and greatly influences the outcome of a propagation cycle. For each net with its own characteristics, it is very important to choose the update function associated with the net in order to get the desired behavior of the neural network. If a wrong update function is given, SNNS will display a error message on your screen. Click <img src="img432.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> in the control panel to select an update function.

The following update functions are available for the various network types:

<img src="img433.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" />

All these functions receive their input from the five update parameter fields in the control panel. See figure [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node40.html#ControlPanel)

The following parameters are required for ART, Hopfield, and Autoassociative networks. The description of the update functions will indicate which parameter is needed.

` `

<img src="img434.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> = vigilance parameter with (<img src="img435.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />) : field1

<img src="img436.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> = initial vigilance parameter for the ART<img src="img437.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> part of the net

with (0 <img src="img438.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> 1) : field1

<img src="img439.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> = vigilance parameter for ART<img src="img440.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> with (<img src="img441.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />) : field2

<img src="img442.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" /> = Inter-ART-Reset control with (<img src="img443.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />) : field3

**a** = strength of the influence of the lower level in F1 by the middle

level with (**a** **\>** 0) : field2

**b** = strength of the influence of the middle level in F1 by the upper

level with (**b** **\>** 0) : field3

**c** = part of the length of vector p with (0 **\<** c **\<** 1) : field4

<img src="img444.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" /> = Kind of threshold with (<img src="img445.gif" data-align="MIDDLE" />) : field5

c = number of units : field1

n = iteration parameter : field1

x = number of selected neurons

Field1..Field5 are the positions in the control panel. For a more detailed description of ART-parameters see section [<img src="icons/cross_ref_motif.gif" data-align="BOTTOM" alt="gif" />](node195.html#artmodelsinsnns): ART Models in SNNS

Now here is a description of the steps the various update functions perform, and of the way in which they differ.

<a href="node55.html" id="tex2html2255"></a> <a href="node53.html" id="tex2html2253"></a> <a href="node53.html" id="tex2html2247"></a> <a href="node1.html" id="tex2html2257"></a> <a href="node390.html" id="tex2html2258"></a>\
